findings.evidence: "The benefits team tracks the stipend budget" (Program Overview); "The finance liaison reviews the stipend budget" (Special Cases); "The people operations office tracks the stipend budget" (Questions and Updates)
findings.fix: Designate a single department responsible for budget tracking and update all three sections to refer to the same entity consistently.
findings.location: Program Overview, Special Cases, and Questions and Updates sections
findings.violation: Three different departments are assigned responsibility for tracking the budget, creating confusion about who actually owns this task.

findings.evidence: "Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time." appears in both sections
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate sentence from one of the sections.
findings.violation: The exact same sentence is repeated in two different sections without adding new information.

findings.evidence: "Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit." appears in both sections
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate sentence from Questions and Updates.
findings.location: Program Overview and Questions and Updates
findings.violation: The sentence is repeated verbatim in two sections, creating redundant content.

findings.evidence: "Employees must submit the receipt, the manager's approval form, and the original purchase order before the review begins."
findings.fix: Remove the purchase order requirement, keeping only the receipt and manager's approval form.
findings.violation: Requiring both a receipt and the original purchase order is redundant; a receipt serves the same documentation purpose.

findings.evidence: "The summary shows the equipment cost and the requested delivery date."
findings.fix: Change to "The summary shows the equipment cost and the purchase date" or remove delivery date reference entirely.
findings.location: How to Apply section, final paragraph
findings.violation: "Requested delivery date" implies the policy covers ordering new equipment, but this is a reimbursement policy for already-purchased items.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: Either specify which types of requests need additional documentation, or change "most requests" to "all requests."
findings.violation: The policy does not clarify what additional documentation is required for requests where a photo is insufficient.

findings.evidence: "Additionally, employees shall retain receipts for one year after the purchase date."
findings.fix: Change to "Additionally, employees must retain receipts for one year after the purchase date."
findings.violation: The word "shall" uses formal legal language inconsistent with the document's conversational tone throughout.

findings.evidence: "The finance office conducts an evaluation of every submitted receipt before it approves the amount."
findings.fix: Rewrite as "The finance office evaluates every submitted receipt and approves the reimbursement amount" or "before they approve the amount."
findings.violation: The pronoun "it" is ambiguous; unclear whether it refers to the finance office or the receipt.

findings.evidence: "The applicant must keep the equipment in good working condition and this office may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Replace "this office" with the specific department name (e.g., "the benefits team" or "the finance office").
findings.violation: "This office" is vague and does not specify which department has the authority to request photo checks.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category."
findings.fix: Break into shorter sentences, e.g., "Employees may request a second device per category if the benefits team confirms the role requires it due to frequent fieldwork. The finance office tracks the second device against the standard annual allocation published in the equipment catalog."
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, second sentence
findings.violation: This is a run-on sentence with multiple nested clauses that is difficult to parse and understand.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Either consistently use third person throughout the document, or clarify who "you" refers to (employee? manager?). Define "stipend item" in plain language.
findings.violation: The section shifts inconsistently between "you" perspective and third person ("Finance reconciles"), and uses undefined jargon like "stipend item."

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Rewrite as "To complete the request, confirm eligibility and upload the receipt" or "Completing the request involves confirming eligibility and uploading the receipt."
findings.violation: Awkward parallel structure mixes a noun phrase with a gerund in an unparallel way.
